nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$, a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, every key of $t$ satisfies $p$ in the recursive sense (the empty tree qualifies, and a node qualifies when its left subtree qualifies, its key satisfies $p$ and its right subtree qualifies) if and only if $p(x)$ holds for every $x$ that is a member of $t$.
nodes.title: A predicate holds at all keys of a binary tree iff it holds at all its members

nodes.summary: For a predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, the empty binary tree satisfies "every key satisfies $p$", and a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ satisfies it exactly when $L$ satisfies it, $p(k)$ holds and $R$ satisfies it.
nodes.title: A predicate holding at every key of a binary tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$ that is ordered (recursively, every key in the left subtree of a node is strictly smaller than the node's key and every key in its right subtree is strictly larger), the comparison search for $x$ in $t$ returns true if and only if $x$ is a member of $t$.
nodes.title: Search in a binary search tree is correct

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, the search for $x$ in $t$ returns a Boolean: false if $t$ is empty, and if $t$ is a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, the search for $x$ in $L$ when $x < k$, the search for $x$ in $R$ when $k < x$, and true otherwise.
nodes.title: Search in a binary search tree

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a key of a linearly ordered type. Deleting $x$ from the empty tree gives the empty tree. Deleting $x$ from a tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ gives the tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ with $x$ deleted and right subtree $R$ if $x < k$; the tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ with $x$ deleted if $k < x$; and the join of $L$ and $R$…
nodes.title: Deletion from a binary search tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, the binary tree built from a list $[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ of elements of $\alpha$ is obtained from the empty tree by inserting $x_n$, then $x_{n-1}$, and so on down to $x_1$, using binary search tree insertion; the empty list gives the empty tree.
nodes.title: Binary search tree built from a list

nodes.summary: For a binary tree $t$ and a list $s$, the accumulated traversal of the empty tree onto $s$ is $s$, and the accumulated traversal of a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ onto $s$ is the accumulated traversal of $L$ onto the list consisting of $k$ followed by the accumulated traversal of $R$ onto $s$.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of a binary tree with an accumulator

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type and $x$ is a key, then the inorder traversal of the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$ is the inorder traversal of $t$ with the first occurrence of $x$ removed (and is the inorder traversal of $t$ itself if $x$ does not occur in it).
nodes.title: Inorder traversal after deletion

nodes.summary: For binary trees $L$ and $R$, the inorder traversal of the join of $L$ and $R$ is the inorder traversal of $L$ followed by the inorder traversal of $R$.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of a join

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$ that is ordered (recursively, every key in the left subtree of a node is strictly smaller than the node's key and every key in its right subtree is strictly larger), the inorder traversal of $t$ is a list with no repeated entries.
nodes.title: The inorder traversal of a binary search tree has no duplicates

nodes.summary: The inorder traversal of a binary tree $t$ is the accumulated inorder traversal of $t$ onto the empty list. Equivalently, the empty tree gives the empty list, and a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ gives the inorder traversal of $L$, then $k$, then the inorder traversal of $R$.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of a binary tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, inserting $x$ into the empty tree gives the single node with key $x$ and empty subtrees; inserting $x$ into a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ inserts $x$ into $L$ when $x < k$, inserts $x$ into $R$ when $k < x$, and returns the node unchanged when $x = k$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a binary search tree

nodes.summary: The join of the empty tree and a tree $R$ is $R$. The join of a tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L_1$ and right subtree $L_2$ and a tree $R$ is the tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L_1$ and right subtree the join of $L_2$ and $R$. Thus, when the first tree is nonempty, $R$ becomes the right subtree of its rightmost node.
nodes.title: Join of two binary trees

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a binary tree over a linearly ordered type, not necessarily ordered, and let $x$ and $y$ be keys with $y \ne x$. If $y$ occurs in $t$, then $y$ occurs in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$.
nodes.title: Deletion keeps the other keys

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type, then for all keys $x$ and $y$, the key $y$ occurs in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$ if and only if $y$ occurs in $t$ and $y \ne x$.
nodes.title: Membership after deletion

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a list $xs$ of elements of $\alpha$, $x$ is a member of the binary tree built from $xs$ by successive binary search tree insertion if and only if $x$ occurs in $xs$.
nodes.title: Members of the binary search tree built from a list

nodes.summary: For every binary tree $T$ and every key $x$, $x$ occurs in the inorder traversal of $T$ if and only if $x$ lies in $T$.
nodes.title: Membership in the inorder traversal of a binary tree

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered. For all keys $x, y$ and every binary tree $T$, $y$ lies in the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ if and only if $y = x$ or $y$ lies in $T$.
nodes.title: Membership after insertion into a binary search tree

nodes.summary: For binary trees $L$ and $R$, a key $x$ occurs in the join of $L$ and $R$ if and only if $x$ occurs in $L$ or $x$ occurs in $R$.
nodes.title: Membership in a join

nodes.summary: A key $x$ belongs to a binary tree $T$ when it is the key of some node of $T$: no key belongs to the empty tree, and $x$ belongs to a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ exactly when $x$ belongs to $L$, $x = k$, or $x$ belongs to $R$.
nodes.title: Membership in a binary tree

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type and $x$ is a key, then $x$ does not occur in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$.
nodes.title: The deleted key is gone

nodes.summary: For every binary tree $T$, the number of nodes of $T$ (each node carries one key, and the empty tree has none) equals the length of the inorder traversal of $T$.
nodes.title: The length of the inorder traversal of a binary tree is its number of nodes

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered, and let $T$ be an ordered binary tree. If a key $x$ lies in $T$, then the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ has the same number of nodes as $T$.
nodes.title: Inserting a present key into a binary search tree leaves its size unchanged

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered. For every binary tree $T$ and every key $x$ that does not lie in $T$, the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ has one more node than $T$.
nodes.title: Inserting an absent key into a binary search tree adds one node

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type, then for every key $x$ the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$ is ordered.
nodes.title: Deletion preserves the search-tree order

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every list $xs$ of elements of $\alpha$, the tree obtained from the empty tree by inserting the elements of $xs$ one at a time, from the last element to the first, is ordered.
nodes.title: Binary search trees built from a list are ordered

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. If a binary tree $T$ over $\alpha$ is ordered, then in the inorder traversal of $T$ every key is less than every key that comes after it.
nodes.title: The inorder traversal of an ordered binary tree is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every key $x \in \alpha$ and every ordered binary tree $T$ over $\alpha$, the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ is ordered.
nodes.title: Binary search tree insertion preserves order

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $R$ be ordered binary search trees over a type with a relation $<$. If $a < b$ for every key $a$ of $L$ and every key $b$ of $R$, then the join of $L$ and $R$ is ordered.
nodes.title: Joining separated ordered trees

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$. The empty tree is ordered, and a binary tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is ordered when $L$ and $R$ are ordered, every key of $L$ is less than $k$, and $k$ is less than every key of $R$.
nodes.title: Ordered binary trees

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, the rank of $x$ in $t$ equals the length of the list obtained from the inorder traversal of $t$ by keeping exactly the entries strictly less than $x$.
nodes.title: Rank counts the smaller inorder entries

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $t$ be a binary search tree with keys in $\alpha$, that is, at every node each key of the left subtree is strictly smaller and each key of the right subtree is strictly larger than the node's key. If selecting index $i$ in $t$ returns a key $x$, then the rank of $x$ in $t$ equals $i$.
nodes.title: The rank of a selected key is its index

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, the rank of $x$ in $t$ is the number of positions of the inorder traversal of $t$ whose entry is strictly less than $x$.
nodes.title: Rank of a key in a binary tree

nodes.summary: For a binary tree $t$ and a natural number $i$, selecting index $i$ in $t$ gives the same result as looking up zero-based position $i$ of the inorder traversal of $t$: the entry at that position when $i$ is less than the length of the traversal, and nothing otherwise.
nodes.title: Selection is indexing into the inorder traversal

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $t$ be a binary search tree with keys in $\alpha$, that is, at every node each key of the left subtree is strictly smaller and each key of the right subtree is strictly larger than the node's key. If $x$ is a key of $t$, then selecting, in $t$, the index equal to the rank of $x$ in $t$ returns $x$.
nodes.title: Selecting the rank of a key returns the key

nodes.summary: For a binary tree $t$ and a natural number $i$, selecting index $i$ in $t$ returns the entry at zero-based position $i$ of the inorder traversal of $t$ when $i$ is less than the length of that traversal, and returns nothing otherwise.
nodes.title: Inorder selection in a binary tree
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
